correctness.rationale: From the exact integral F0=(A(xi)-exp(-i eta)A(xi-eta))/(i eta), differentiation at every lambda=(2 pi m,2 pi n), mn(m-n) nonzero, yields F0_xi=i/(k(k-l)), F0_eta=-i/(l(k-l)), and F0(lambda(1+t))=t^2/2+O(t^3). The imaginary component is transverse to the added s coordinate. Applying the analytic implicit-function theorem yields the real residual t^2/2+epsilon Re G(lambda)+O(t^3+abs(epsilon*t)+epsilon^2), with strictly positive second t derivative. Its minimum sign proves exactly 2 or 0 local real zeros and simple two-root Jacobians. Affine coefficients follow exactly by frequency differentiation. The 3/4 asymptotic is the area fraction of two wedges totaling 3 pi/2, with O(R) lattice-boundary error. The standalone numerical checker was actually executed with successful derivative and pair-root checks, but finite tests do not establish the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The triangle's discrete unweighted Fourier zeros control pairwise orthogonality of exponentials. The new classification determines exactly how each lattice orthogonality constraint behaves under arbitrary small bounded positive-density perturbations: signed creation or annihilation of two simple zeros, universal square-root displacement, and an explicit arithmetic coefficient for affine weights. The natural coordinate weight yields a sharp 3:1 angular law across infinitely many nodes. These are structural, motivated, potentially useful for weighted spectral-measure stability, and do not follow merely by restating the known unweighted zero lattice.
